_note: Boxes are NORMALISED to the tile (0-1). CENTRE OF THE SUMMIT BAND, second row, and it is the ONE TILE OF THE THREE WITH A DEPTH LADDER: distant forested peaks across the top-left, an empty band of mist through the middle-left, and the first genuinely NEAR trees along the bottom edge. Read it as three storeys. TOP-LEFT (x 0-0.40, y 0-0.68) is a forested massif and it is the densest real foliage in the summit band -- rank after rank of tall trees with unmistakable vertical trunks and flat spreading crowns marching along ridge crests, with blue-green wash pooled behind them; five separate stands are boxed. MIDDLE-LEFT (x 0-0.44, y 0.68-0.92) is nearly bare silk, mist between the far peaks and the near ground, and nothing in it may be selected; a very faint pale structure near (0.32,0.72) may be a distant pavilion but is too indistinct to name. BOTTOM (y 0.80-1.0) is the near ground and is drawn in a completely different register: at x 0.63-0.79 there is a big deciduous tree with an OCHRE TRUNK AND BRANCHES clearly visible under a canopy of drooping outlined leaf clusters washed blue-green -- the only tree in these three tiles whose wood is drawn as a coloured solid rather than a stroke, and by far the best hinge subject here; beside it at x 0.29-0.50 stands an autumn tree of round outlined leaves (圈葉) filled ORANGE-RED, and at x 0.49-0.59 a dark pine. THE DECOYS, and this tile has the worst of them. (1) The rounded dome across the top-right (x 0.62-1.0, y 0-0.28) carries a broad flat BLUE-GREEN MINERAL WASH (石青) -- it is a distant peak painted blue, not water and not leaves, and it is the single most dangerous surface for a colour-based foliage pass in the whole scroll, because it is the same pigment family used on the canopies. (2) The ridge at x 0.42-0.75, y 0.60-0.80 is smothered in 点苔 moss dots and short scrub strokes with NO trunk anywhere in it, and it carries a dotted contour chain along its foot at about y 0.73 -- dots on stone. (3) The cliffs at x 0.75-0.94, y 0.63-0.88 hang in long vertical hemp-fibre strokes that read as drooping needles; bare rock. (4) The great pale massif right of centre (x 0.60-0.95, y 0.20-0.60) is empty stone drawn in contour outline only and should score zero. Content continues into t004 on the left, t006 on the right, t009 below.

objects.name: forest on the top-left crest
objects.note: a rank of tall trees along a crest, trunks drawn as separate dark verticals under flat crowns, blue-green wash behind. Clean silhouette against the pale slope below; the top of the box is where the crowns break the crest line

objects.name: forest on the crest above centre-left
objects.note: clipped by the top edge and continuing into t001. Crowns and trunks both legible; the crowns silhouette against bare silk, so the upper mask boundary is unambiguous

objects.name: forest on the ridge right of the top-centre crest
objects.note: a third rank stepping right and slightly down; same construction. Split from forest-crest-top-centre only so the mask does not sweep the pale rock notch between the two crests

objects.name: forest on the slope below the upper crests
objects.note: the densest of the far stands, with a distinct blue-green wash filling the gaps between trunks. Below y 0.23 the slope becomes bare radiating hemp-fibre stroke -- hold the bottom edge

objects.name: wooded knoll, left of centre
objects.note: THE LARGEST FOLIAGE MASS IN THE SUMMIT BAND. A whole knoll covered in trees: overlapping dabbed crowns with blue-green wash, individual trunks still findable through the mass at x 0.14-0.16 and x 0.24-0.27. SEARCH REGION nonetheless -- the knoll's own rock shows through in the lower-left of the box and along its right shoulder, perhaps 30% of the pixels. Refine per-pixel; do not use raw

objects.name: treeline on the lower ridge below the knoll
objects.note: a long rank of pines and broadleaf trees on a lower crest, trunks clearly separated and standing against pale ground -- one of the cleanest bands in the tile. Its right end at about x 0.45 is where the moss-dotted decoy ridge begins; do not extend past it

objects.name: tree crowns capping the right-hand peak
objects.note: genuine crowns with blue-green wash sitting on the summit of the right-hand rock spur, breaking its silhouette. The spur BELOW them (rock-cliff-vertical-strokes-right) is the decoy this box must not bleed into -- the boundary is sharp, at the base of the crowns

objects.name: big deciduous tree, near ground, right of centre
objects.note: THE BEST SUBJECT IN THIS TILE. A near tree drawn at full scale: a solid OCHRE trunk with two heavy limbs radiating right and down-left, and a canopy of drooping outlined leaf clusters filled with blue-green wash hanging off them. Because the wood is a coloured solid and the leaves are outlined glyphs, they separate cleanly by colour -- cut the ochre limbs out of the mask and hinge the leaf clusters about them. Do NOT displace the trunk

objects.name: orange autumn tree, bottom centre
objects.note: a near tree of round double-outlined leaves (圈葉) filled with an ORANGE-RED wash, clipped by the bottom edge and continuing into t009. The only warm-coloured foliage in the summit band, so it is trivially separable by hue -- but note the inverse trap: a mask built to find 'not green' foliage will also grab warm-washed ROCK elsewhere in the scroll. Restrict warm-hue foliage rules to this box

objects.name: dark pine, bottom centre
objects.note: a single dark pine with a clearly drawn vertical trunk and tiered horizontal needle-sprays, standing between the autumn tree and the big deciduous. Clipped by the bottom edge. Small but structurally unambiguous -- trunk and leaf both visible

objects.name: sparse thin trees, bottom centre-left
objects.note: two or three slender near trees with thin bare trunks and only a scattering of leaf dabs on their upper branches -- nearly winter-bare. leavesVisible is true but the leaf fraction is low; a sway here will look like the branches moving, not a canopy, which may or may not be wanted. Clipped by the bottom edge

objects.name: tree stand, bottom right corner
objects.note: a group of dark pines and broadleaf trees with visible trunks filling the corner, clipped by both the right and bottom edges and continuing into t006 and t009. Denser and nearer than anything above it in the tile

objects.name: blue-washed rock dome, top right
objects.note: THE WORST DECOY IN THE SUMMIT BAND. A rounded distant peak carrying a broad flat blue-green MINERAL wash (石青) across its far side, with moss dots along its contour. It is the same pigment family Wang Meng uses on the canopies, so any rule of the form 'blue-green wash means foliage' selects this entire dome and swings a mountain. The separator is texture, not colour: this wash is FLAT and unbroken over a large smooth area, while a canopy wash is always broken up by leaf glyphs and crown edges. NEVER animate

objects.name: hemp-fibre slopes under the upper-left forests
objects.note: the stone the top-left forests stand on: pale slopes drawn with short radiating 牛毛皴 strokes fanning downhill, which at reduced size mimic needle sprays. Interleaves with the bottoms of the forest boxes above it -- that overlap is why those boxes cannot be tight

objects.name: great pale slope, centre
objects.note: a large, nearly empty rock face descending from the upper crests, contour lines and faint stroke only. A control surface: if a foliage mask fires anywhere in here, the threshold is wrong

objects.name: pale massif right of centre
objects.note: outline-drawn rock with almost no interior texture -- long looping contours and a scatter of dots along the edges. Rigid

objects.name: moss-dotted ridge, centre below the knoll
objects.note: MAJOR DECOY. A ridge and its valley smothered edge to edge in 点苔 moss dots and short scrub strokes, dense enough to read as a wooded hillside at any reduced size. Examined at full resolution there is not one trunk and not one crown silhouette anywhere in it, and a single-file chain of dots runs along its foot at about y 0.73 marking a rock contour. Dots on stone. kind:rock, leavesVisible:false, NEVER animate -- this is the exact texture that got the previous automatic pass rejected

objects.name: cliff with hanging vertical strokes, right
objects.note: DECOY. The body of the right-hand spur below tree-crowns-peak-right, plus a long dark vertical gully at about x 0.87-0.92 -- all drawn in hanging vertical hemp-fibre strokes that mimic drooping needles or vines. Bare stone. The boundary with the real crowns above it is sharp and must be respected

objects.name: dark cliff at the right edge
objects.note: a narrow dark rock face clipped by the right edge, continuing into t006. Heavy dabbing along its contour is moss, not leaf

objects.name: bare silk mist between the far peaks and the near ground
objects.note: an almost untouched band of silk separating the summit storey from the near ground -- the depth cue that makes the near trees below read as near. A very faint pale structure sits near (0.32, 0.72) that may be a distant pavilion in mist; it is too indistinct to classify and is left inside the void rather than guessed at. Nothing in this box may be selected as foliage
